hypothesis: Empirical cross-subject and cross-muscle validation of local bioenergetics model can be achieved without verified raw human time-series.

hypothesis: Hug et al. 2021 reported Gastrocnemius Medialis discharge rates of 9.8, 12.6, 15.4, and 19.8 Hz across 8 independent human participants.
result: Refuted: Table 2 of Hug et al. 2021 preprint and journal publication reports GM mean discharge rates of 8.1, 8.1, 7.6, and 12.2 pps after manual editing. The eight operators were rater co-authors evaluating shared recordings from an unknown number of male participants across two reused experiments. N=8 raters != 8 subjects.
impact: Retracted unconfirmed discharge rates; replaced with published Table 2 numbers; classified biological sample size as UNKNOWN; barred equating operators with independent biological subjects.

hypothesis: More than 99% of energy in a 45-minute 250 W whole-body test is supplied oxidatively based on the ratio of single-muscle static PCr buffer to external mechanical work.
result: Refuted: Dividing single-muscle local PCr buffer capacity (0.62 kJ) by whole-body external mechanical work (675 kJ) commits a category error between static local capacity and dynamic whole-body flux, confounds mechanical work with gross metabolic expenditure (~3375 kJ), and ignores systemic anaerobic glycolysis (~75 kJ) and multi-muscle recruitment.
impact: Enforces multi-dimensional energetic accounting separating mechanical work, metabolic cost, ATP turnover, oxidative resynthesis, and glycolysis; bars invalid >99% oxidative claims for TARGET-CPE45.

hypothesis: Nominal exercise protocol timing (fitting from 90s nominal stop) reproduces true recovery kinetics, prospective prediction from t=90s is achievable without workload/perfusion data, model M2 validates multi-scale physiological balance, intracellular pH universally satisfies pH >= 6.86, and arbitrary MR signal amplitudes can identify absolute resting PCr concentration and active muscle volume.
result: Refuted across multiple dimensions: (1) Fitting from nominal 90s stop instead of actual biochemical nadir contaminates recovery with ongoing exercise depletion, underestimating k by 20-33% and degrading fit quality; (2) Prospective prediction (Scenario B) from t=90s prior to observing future nadir and post-exercise lag is blocked (PROSPECTIVE_PREDICTION_BLOCKED_UNOBSERVED_DEPLETION_DYNAMICS) because depletion depth and duration cannot be inferred without work rate or perfusion data; (3) Model M2 is mathematically a constrained monoexponential baseline model, not a validated multi-scale physiological ODE; full model M3 cannot be executed on relative MRS alone (M3_NOT_EXECUTABLE_ON_AVAILABLE_OBSERVATIONS); (4) Universal non-acidosis claim pH >= 6.86 is refuted by calculated minimum pH of 6.7932 in Trial 1 (range 6.7932-7.0228); (5) Arbitrary MR signal amplitudes are intrinsically scale-confounded with receiver coil sensitivity and cannot identify absolute mM concentration; (6) Single-coil MRS creates an exact unidentifiable scaling symmetry between active muscle volume and localized metabolic depletion; (7) Cross-subject LOSO validation is mathematically impossible on an N=1 cohort.
impact: Mandates empirical nadir detection for phase alignment; blocks prospective forward simulation without work rate/perfusion inputs; reclassifies M2 as constrained monoexponential; marks M3 as unexecutable on available data; retracts pH >= 6.86; maintains absolute PCr concentration and active volume as strictly unidentifiable; prohibits cross-subject generalization from single-participant MRS.

hypothesis: Successful multi-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out validation of macroscopic aerobic bioenergetic coupling (P_mech -> VO2) on cycle ergometry constitutes empirical validation of the full multi-scale physiological ODE (M3), identifies localized intracellular high-energy phosphate dynamics ([PCr], [Pi], [ATP], cytosolic pH), validates motor unit recruitment order, and validates extreme 45-minute survival (TARGET-CPE45).
result: Refuted: Whole-body pulmonary oxygen consumption and crank mechanical power represent volume-integrated macroscopic observables. By the many-to-one mapping (entanglement fallacy), an infinite manifold of localized muscle recruitment patterns, regional perfusion states, and intracellular phosphate depletion curves yield the identical systemic VO2 curve. Therefore, ACTES CPET data strictly cannot identify localized [PCr], [Pi], or pH dynamics (which remain bounded by Rehman 2024 N=1), cannot observe motor unit discharge rates (which remain bounded by Hug 2021), and cannot validate TARGET-CPE45, which requires a dedicated continuous 45-minute endurance test rather than a 15-minute incremental graded ramp to exhaustion.
impact: Prevents false claims of full physiological model validation. Strictly confines ACTES validation to macroscopic aerobic efficiency (eta_gross) and Phase II response kinetics (tau). Establishes REMAINING_BARRIERS_MATRIX and maintains TARGET-CPE45 as NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED and biological interventions as NO_GO.

hypothesis: Single-variable linear body mass scaling (P/M) universally improves prediction across all individual human subjects, and macroscopic cycling efficiency parameters (delta efficiency eta_delta, regression slope beta1) directly transfer to running locomotion without modality-specific calibration via an ad-hoc linear velocity-to-power multiplier.
result: Refuted on two empirical grounds: (1) In the ACTES cycling cohort (EXP-0043), while linear mass normalization improves macro-average R2 across the full cohort, it worsens prediction RMSE in 7 of the 18 participants (Subjects 3, 4, 6, 15, 16, 17, 18), demonstrating that simple linear mass scaling introduces individual bias for light endurance and heavy muscular athletes; (2) In the Malaga treadmill cohort (EXP-0044, N=981 valid tests across N=846 independent participants), applying the naive formula pred_vo2 = 560 + (7.657 * 25.0) * speed incurs a severe error penalty (GroupKFold RMSE = 584.9 mL/min, R2 = 0.2465, RMSE penalty = +180.8 mL/min vs M4). This failure is classified as AD_HOC_CROSS_MODAL_MAPPING_FAILURE because the 25 W/(km/h) factor is an arbitrary construct rather than measured running mechanical power. True physical cross-modal transfer is classified as PHYSICAL_CROSS_MODAL_TRANSFER_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE due to lack of mechanical power, ground reaction forces, and tendon elastic recoil data.
impact: Prohibits universal application of uncalibrated linear body mass scaling without individual body composition accounting; bars arbitrary linear conversion of running speed to cycling mechanical power; reclassifies cross-modal transfer failure into AD_HOC_CROSS_MODAL_MAPPING_FAILURE and sets PHYSICAL_CROSS_MODAL_TRANSFER_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE; mandates modality-specific biomechanical locomotion models.

hypothesis: Single-muscle vastus lateralis knee extension torque, sEMG amplitude, and ultrasound fascicle length directly predict whole-body maximum strength and athletic capacity, and successful validation of 20-minute intermittent fatigue compensation models provides empirical validation for continuous 45-minute extreme metabolic endurance (TARGET-CPE45).
result: Refuted on three physiological and biomechanical grounds: (1) Decoupling in Dynamic Motion: Active joint torque cannot be inferred from static sEMG (R2 = 0.118 on active points, pub 0.13) or static fascicle strain (R2 = 0.016 on active points, pub 0.01), refuting static muscle proxy models. (2) Indeterminacy of Net Joint Moment: Knee dynamometer torque (N*m) conflates four distinct quadriceps heads, antagonist hamstring co-contraction, and variable patellar tendon moment arm (3.5 to 4.8 cm); converting joint torque to single-muscle force requires unobserved load-sharing assumptions. (3) Protocol and Epistemic Incommensurability: Neuromuscular compensation (+26% activation increase at 45% MVC) over 20 minutes of intermittent contractions does not measure intracellular high-energy phosphate depletion ([PCr], [ATP], [Pi]), cytosolic acidosis (pH), or whole-body metabolic heat flux, and strictly cannot validate continuous 45-minute steady-state extreme endurance (TARGET-CPE45, 2700 s at 250 W). TARGET-CPE45 remains NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED and biological interventions strictly NO_GO.
impact: Prohibits using isolated single-muscle dynamometry or static proxies to extrapolate whole-body performance; prohibits claiming that 20-minute submaximal fatigue validates continuous 45-minute extreme endurance TARGET-CPE45; preserves strict epistemic boundaries on tissue-level vs whole-body observables.

hypothesis: Raw UWB radar frequency reflection features directly generalize across unseen human subjects to predict knee extension torque (%MVC) without subject-specific calibration, and single engineered composite feature M4 provides a superior cross-subject predictive model over simple linear sEMG baseline M1.
result: Refuted across two rigorous empirical evaluations on Bird et al. (2026) raw dynamic arrays (DATA_Dynamic_Knee.mat, 3,226 observations, N=6; torque in fraction of MVC [0.0, 1.0], partitioned into 1,382 passive protocol and 1,844 active protocol observations): (1) Radar Generalization Collapse: The specific uncalibrated UWB Ridge regression model (204 frequency channels) collapses from intra-participant 5-fold CV R2 = 0.9763 +/- 0.0097 to cross-subject Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) R2 = -2.4457 +/- 2.2077 (NRMSE = 47.25%), failing on 5 of 6 held-out human participants. Comprehensive sensitivity analysis confirms that this collapse persists across all Ridge regularizations (alpha from 0.001 to 1000), inner-fold standard/robust scalers, frequency subsets (S11 R2 = -0.8431, S21 R2 = -9.5060, Mag R2 = -0.7495, Phase R2 = -2.5501), and active protocol runs (R2 = -6.0154). This collapse is confined to this linear Ridge implementation and must not be extrapolated to declare all UWB technologies unusable, nor to non-linear architectures (LME, LSTM, RF) without explicit LOSO validation. (2) Engineered Feature M4 Evaluation: Cross-subject LOSO evaluation of the single engineered feature model M4 (R2 = 0.3251 +/- 0.0946, NRMSE = 21.93%) yields only a statistically insignificant +0.0148 delta R2 over standard Hill model M3 (R2 = 0.3103 +/- 0.0819; paired t = 1.080, p = 0.3294, 95% CI [-0.0204, +0.0501]), which does NOT prove equivalence. Relative to M1 sEMG baseline (R2 = 0.4628 +/- 0.0651), the observed sample point-estimate favors M1 by +0.1377 (Delta R2 = -0.1377), but this difference is NOT statistically significant at two-sided alpha=0.05 (paired t = -2.462, p = 0.0571; Wilcoxon p = 0.0625; 95% CI [-0.2814, +0.0061] spans zero) due to limited power (N=6). The negative result is formally designated ENGINEERED_FEATURE_M4_NO_VERIFIED_ADVANTAGE. The full multi-scale physiological ODE architecture of SUBJECT-01 is NOT evaluated in this linear feature test and remains unfalsified (FULL_SUBJECT01_MULTISCALE_ARCHITECTURE_NOT_FALSIFIED_BY_THIS_TEST).
impact: Bars claiming cross-subject generalizability for raw uncalibrated UWB radar; bars declaring engineered feature M4 superior to baseline sEMG M1 on raw human dynamometry (ENGINEERED_FEATURE_M4_NO_VERIFIED_ADVANTAGE); preserves FULL_SUBJECT01_MULTISCALE_ARCHITECTURE_NOT_FALSIFIED_BY_THIS_TEST; mandates subject-specific calibration for RF-based biomechanical models; preserves negative result in repository registry.

hypothesis: An isolated +20% increase in contractile muscle fiber force directly yields a +20% increase in net functional joint torque without neural co-activation tuning or pennation angle losses.
result: MODEL_ONLY. With fixed gamma and all other scenario assumptions, a +2.8 degree pennation change lowers cos(alpha) by 1.38% relative to nominal. Simulated +20% fiber force yields +18.34% net knee torque. The 8.3% is the share of the planned torque gain lost under this scenario.
impact: Treat geometry and antagonist moment separately. Their empirical dose-response and necessity for meeting the target remain unverified.

result: Comprehensive global audit across Zenodo, Dryad, Figshare, PhysioNet, SimTK, AddBiomechanics, and UCI identified 0 qualified datasets. Bird 2026 lacked antagonists; Wang 2022 used locomotion with inverse-dynamics moments; UCI 278 lacked torque transducers. Experiment E1 is DATA_BLOCKED.

result: Comprehensive audit identified 0 qualified datasets. Kongsgaard et al. (2007) deposited only aggregate cohort means (104, 118, 127 mm2); raw individual data was never deposited. Substituting literature means as individual data is prohibited as unscientific. Experiment E2 is DATA_BLOCKED.
impact: HYP-0010 remains unverified. Tendon stress concentration at the proximal insertion (38.46 MPa baseline, 46.15 MPa at +20% force) confirmed theoretically, causing an estimated 60-75% reduction in cyclic fatigue life.

hypothesis: An independent third public human adult MTJ transcriptomic dataset exists to replicate the frozen MTJCore myonuclear program.
result: Systematic audit across GEO, ArrayExpress, CELLxGENE, and GSA-Human identified 0 open independent cohorts outside Copenhagen. E-MTAB-12529 is discovery; E-MTAB-15400 already failed in Stage 6 (0.5818 < 0.60); E-MTAB-12530 has identical donors; HRA002803 is controlled-access. Experiment E5 is DATA_BLOCKED.
impact: MTJCore cannot be claimed as a replicated universal marker of tissue strength. Directional RNA concordance does not equal protein translation or mechanical tensile strength.

title: Failure of Uncalibrated Surface Antagonist EMG to Improve Cross-Subject Isometric Torque Estimation
statement: Adding uncalibrated antagonist hamstrings surface EMG (M2) to an agonist-only OLS model (M1) failed to achieve statistically significant improvement in Leave-One-Subject-Out prediction error across 20 adults (Delta RMSE = -3.94 Nm, paired t-test p = 0.1426, Wilcoxon p = 0.2863).
reason: Antagonist co-activation magnitude is low (~8-11% of agonist amplitude) and subject to inter-individual skin impedance variance, causing unregularized cross-subject models to fit individual noise.

title: Impossibility of Mechanical Stress Determination in Bogaerts Cohort Due to Absent Layer CSA
statement: Full mechanical validation of HYP-0010 (regional stress distribution) was blocked in Bogaerts et al. (2017) because individual sub-tendon cross-sectional areas were not measured, preventing conversion of force into engineering stress.
reason: Ultrasound imaging was restricted to sagittal 2D displacement tracking without transverse axial sub-tendon morphometry.

title: Inability to Replicate Myonuclear MTJCore Program on Oxford Achilles Single-Cell Atlas
statement: Attempted replication of Karlsen's myonuclear MTJCore signature on Cohen et al. (2026) was blocked due to cell-type boundary: Cohen et al. dissociated and isolated tendon fibroblasts/tenocytes only, with zero myonuclei present in the dataset.
reason: Surgical dissection protocols removed skeletal muscle myofibers to enrich for tendon fibroblasts, precluding myonuclear evaluation.

title: Falsification of Surface EMG Predictive Value in Cross-Subject Population Models
statement: Adding surface EMG features to anthropometric and kinematic variables increased cross-subject prediction error across all tested algorithms (OLS and Ridge), with antagonist EMG significantly degrading RMSE (p = 0.0089).
reason: Subcutaneous adipose filtering and skin impedance differences create inter-individual noise that overwhelms the small co-activation torque signal.

title: Falsification of Layer-Specific Active Tendon Strain Heterogeneity at Subject Level
statement: Subject-level aggregation (N=10) of Bogaerts ultrasound speckle tracking during isometric plantarflexion refuted the hypothesis of layer-dependent strain differences (Friedman chi2 = 0.80, p = 0.6703).
reason: Prior claims of strain heterogeneity in Cycle 16 were an artifact of 4-fold pseudoreplication treating repeated trials as independent subjects.

title: Inability to Replicate MTJCore on Oxford Single-Cell Atlas Due to Missing Donor Pseudobulk Tables
statement: Independent replication of the frozen Karlsen MTJCore signature on Cohen et al. (2026) was blocked because public DEG tables isolate fibroblast subtypes and lack donor-level myonuclear pseudobulk counts.
reason: Primary study prioritized stromal fibroblast specialization and did not provide donor-level non-junctional control contrast matrices.

title: Oxford Achilles Atlas Ineligible for Third Independent Replication of MTJCore
statement: Independent biological replication of MTJCore on the Oxford Achilles Atlas is invalid due to dataset identity with the discovery training cohort (100% data leakage). In the global public domain, no third independent snRNA-seq cohort with donor-level adult human MTJ contrasts exists. MTJCore replication attempts on Cohen et al. are closed with decision STOP_NO_ADDED_SCIENTIFIC_VALUE.
reason: Data provenance audit proved that Cohen et al. (2026) was the original discovery cohort of MTJCore.

title: Stromal COL22A1 Upregulation Fails Preregistered Donor Consistency Threshold
statement: In the Achilles MTJ-vs-midbody fibroblast contrast, COL22A1 upregulation achieved a donor direction consistency of only 0.60 (elevated in 3 of 5 donors), failing the preregistered threshold of >= 0.75 and resulting in rejection from the frozen fibroblast signature. Hypothesis HYP-0013 lacks novelty as cellular distributions were already published in Cohen et al. (2026).
reason: Inter-donor inconsistency in stromal COL22A1 expression and lack of originality relative to published literature.

title: Isomass Pennation Scaling Trade-Off: Force Gain Sacrifices Shortening Velocity and Range of Motion
statement: In human skeletal muscle under fixed total mass/volume (isomass constraint), increasing pennation angle theta from 14 deg to 18 deg increases PCSA and isometric force by +25.2% (from 6059 N to 7586 N), but causes an unavoidable geometric reduction of -21.7% in maximum shortening velocity (v_max drops from 8.84 to 6.92 l_0/s) and joint active range of motion due to reduced fiber length l_f. Pure pennation remodeling cannot achieve +20% force without dynamic performance penalties.
reason: Constant-volume geometric constraint: V = PCSA * l_f = const. Increasing PCSA proportionally shortens fascicle length l_f, reducing the number of sarcomeres in series and maximum shortening speed.

title: Tendon Elastic Modulus Remodeling Without Hypertrophy Yields Zero Fatigue Life Gain
statement: Under a +20% augmented muscle force, increasing tendon elastic modulus E by +15% without cross-sectional area hypertrophy (Delta CSA = 0) produces exactly 0% improvement in cyclic fatigue life (N_cycles remains 0.133x baseline, -86.7% loss). While tendon stiffness increases, peak engineering tensile stress sigma = F / CSA remains unattenuated at 48.74 MPa, proving that material stiffening without geometric hypertrophy is ineffective for tendon fatigue protection.
reason: Wöhler S-N fatigue life is governed by cyclic peak tensile stress sigma relative to ultimate tensile strength UTS. Altering elastic modulus affects strain at load but leaves stress identical if CSA is unchanged.

title: Falsification of Isolated In Vivo Specific Tension Identifiability from Joint Dynamometry Without Subject-Specific Volumetry
statement: Global uncertainty quantification (Monte Carlo N=10,000) across anthropometric, kinematic, and allometric parameters revealed that in vivo specific tension calculated from joint dynamometry alone has a 95% credibility interval of [17.58, 44.98] N/cm2 (uncertainty span 27.41 N/cm2). Specific tension cannot be claimed as an independently measured scalar for individual subjects without co-acquired 3D-MRI muscle volumetry, B-mode ultrasound fascicle tracking, and interpolated twitch activation measurements.
reason: Dynamometer net joint torque reflects an indeterminate product of moment arm, muscle volume, fascicle length, pennation, antagonist co-contraction, and central voluntary drive.

title: Falsification of Fine-Scale Biological Equivalence Between Sexes in Muscle Specific Tension at 10% Margin
statement: Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) on N=20 adults (10 males, 10 females, DPValid) failed to establish statistical equivalence of quadriceps specific tension at a +/- 10% equivalence margin (p_TOST = 0.1449 > 0.05). While Welch's t-test yielded p = 0.8981 (failing to reject equality of means: male 26.27 vs female 26.55 N/cm2), concluding biological equivalence requires an expanded statistical power. Equivalence is statistically supported only at a broader +/- 20% margin (p_TOST = 0.0169).
reason: Failure to reject a null hypothesis of difference in a Student's t-test does not constitute proof of equivalence.

title: External Bilateral Leg Press Cohort Absence (DATA_BLOCKED), Naive Pseudoinverse Incompatibility, and Inconclusive Single-Joint DPValid Precision
statement: Open search and gate audit across 6 candidate repositories (OpenCap, Zoger 2025, Zushi 2024, Zenodo 6503956, Figshare 33936784/PLOS 0357488, Zenodo 23979972/Frontiers 1948872) yielded 0 admitted cohorts for external validation of bilateral isometric leg press (Outcome 4: DATA_BLOCKED). Naive 3-DOF closed-chain assignment (a=0.95) is physically incompatible (point-contact overdetermination residual 253.68 Nm at 100 deg; flat-foot COP = +0.1706 m > +0.16 m boundary). On single-joint DPValid (N=20), all pairwise paired cluster bootstrap 95% CIs relative to proposed Delta_min = 0.08 cross the threshold (M2 vs F0 [+0.0259, +0.1428], M2 vs M1 [-0.0903, +0.1173], Outcome 3: INCONCLUSIVE).
reason: Zoger 2025 raw data are available upon request only; allometric volume regression is nearly collinear with age/mass/height/sex on N=20 participants.

title: Heterochrony Damage Spike Under TARGET-ADAPT25 and Ballistic 100% MVC Enthesis Margin Breach Under Rapid dF/dt
statement: Accelerating muscular adaptation speed (+25%, tau_m = 12 d) ahead of slow tendon collagen remodeling (tau_t = 90 d) induces a transient 2.94x peak daily fatigue damage spike around week 3.0 (48 days > 2.0x baseline hazard). At maximal 100% MVC ballistic tension (7661 N, dF/dt = 20,000 N/s), localized deep-layer enthesis von Mises stress reaches 92.20 MPa (> 85 MPa collagen threshold, SF_local = 1.03) unadapted, and remains at 79.91 MPa (SF_local = 1.31 < 1.50 safety gate) even after Case 2C (+15% CSA, +10% UTS).
reason: Tendon collagen turnover half-life limits safe adaptation velocity (BLOCKER-03), and deep-layer shear concentration + viscoelastic rate stiffening erode nominal uniaxial safety margins (BLOCKER-02).

title: Continuous +20% Work Thermal Breach Across Climates and AEGIS-01 Evaporative Barrier Penalty
statement: Continuous unpaced output at 360 W (1436.3 W total heat) breaches the 39.5 C core safety limit across all tested climates >= 20 C within 1240 to 2365 s (reaching 39.81 C at 20 C and 42.77 C at 35 C), while 300 W breaches 39.5 C in all warm/hot climates >= 28 C (1625 to 2335 s). Imposing the AEGIS-01 keratinized barrier (-35% skin evaporative/convective conductance, +2 kg) cuts safe temperate duty cycle capacity D_max by -14.0% at 300 W (1.00 -> 0.86) and -25.0% at 360 W (0.92 -> 0.69), confirming PR #9 CONDITIONAL HOLD.
reason: Human evaporative cooling capacity (~580-750 W effective ceiling with sweat drip) cannot sustain continuous 1200-1450 W metabolic heat loads.

title: Equal-work control removes the large thermal contrast
statement: At identical external work, the modeled intermittent minus constant peak core difference is -0.058 to +0.001 C across reported conditions and time steps; the sign changes in the temperate scenario. Equal-work pairs all pass the archived model gate. No model-independent or functional benefit is established.
reason: Original full-power comparator changes scheduled work, while results at equal work are small and partly sensitive to model or time step.

title: Frozen Pennes model loses to persistence on held-out light cycling
statement: 35 sessions from 6 participants. Participant-average MAE is 0.429 C for the unchanged model vs 0.251 C for persistence, paired base-minus-model bootstrap 95% CI [-0.286, -0.080] C. Limited transfer gate fails at all tested humidity assumptions.
reason: Scope is the locked initial state and parameterization on a protocol-shift dataset; starting tissue temperatures, actual mechanical traces and humidity were unavailable. No inference about 2700-s performance.

title: Cross-protocol first-two-sprint model fails against persistence
statement: Training the late-sprint ratio model on Chmura and applying to 21 previously viewed Jutlah participants gives participant-weighted MAE 138.98 W against 95.36 W for first-sprint persistence. Paired MAE difference persistence minus linear [-80.41,-10.07] W. Within-cohort LOSO intervals cross zero.
reason: Different rest intervals, populations and task context are confounded; no unique causal mechanism inferred.

title: Exercise-rest cognitive response contrasts inconclusive
statement: For 71 participants, mean paired exercise-minus-rest change in correct-response latency was +2.02 ms, bootstrap CI [-7.10,11.59], and accuracy change -0.0041, CI [-0.0221,0.0106]. Neither superiority nor equivalence is established.
reason: Both intervals include zero, and prespecified functional equivalence margins are absent. This task does not evaluate locomotion or 45-minute performance.

title: Adding knee velocity does not improve the tested linear moment model
statement: On 12 held-out participants, angle-minus-angle-and-velocity MAE differences in source units had bootstrap 95% CIs [-0.000798,0.000089] for 0 lb and [-0.001143,-0.000092] for 25 lb. Inverse-dynamics moment units remain unresolved; ISS-0028.
reason: Limited to two simple linear models, a single young cohort and task; no inference that dynamic effects do not exist.

title: Independent inverse dynamics does not resolve the moment scale in both participants
statement: AB01 reconstructed moment/source slope divided by mass is 1.089; AB02 is 0.574. Both meet prespecified angle and correlation quality gates, but AB02 does not meet either Nm or Nm/kg scale gate. ISS-0028 remains open.
reason: Only two participants and reconstructed processing; author processing, force assignment, filtering, and possible scale differences require verification.

title: Late 15-minute thermal forecast has no demonstrated advantage over persistence
statement: For the 60–45 min increment, MAE is 0.329 C for continued variable-power Pennes vs 0.250 C persistence; paired persistence-minus-model MAE CI [-0.198, 0.026] C includes zero.
reason: Same previously reviewed cohort, assumed power timestamps, sparse ambient inputs, and different model initialization and measurement-site definitions.

title: Cross-protocol nominal force has no established advantage over cohort mean
statement: Unfitted EXP-0061 100-degree baseline predicts 11 Santos W0 peak forces at MAE 486.4 N versus 508.8 N for leave-one-person-out mean; paired mean difference [−36.1,85.2] N includes zero.
reason: Approximate 110-degree task and apparatus differ from model; individual geometry and mass unavailable. Does not reject model in its original domain.

title: Knee-angle matching alone fails to establish improved force prediction
statement: On the previously viewed Santos cohort, nominal 110-degree model MAE 631.9 N vs 486.4 N at 100 degrees and 508.8 N for participant-held-out mean. Both paired intervals include zero; prespecified superiority for 110 degrees is not established.
reason: Other geometry, individual anthropometry, and independent hip posture response are absent; this is a reused sample, not a formal test of the whole architecture.

title: Archived force chain gravity does not match its stated potential energy
statement: At knee angles 100/110/140 degrees the archived hip gravity term differs from the central finite difference of its documented potential by 9.04/9.57/10.73 Nm. Correcting only this line changes strategy 2 gain at 100 degrees from 21.64% to 21.93%.
reason: The variable dV_dphi1 already includes the shank and foot terms; dV_dphi2 is added again to the hip generalized moment.

title: Gravity correction does not establish force-prediction superiority on reused cohort
statement: For 11 previously viewed participants, corrected 100-degree MAE is 477.1 N and corrected 110-degree MAE 613.6 N against participant-held-out mean 508.8 N; paired intervals against baseline include zero.
reason: Same small cohort, no individual geometry or body mass, approximate task angle and unknown hip configuration; bootstrap retains correlated LOSO predictions. No conclusion on exact model validity.

title: Historical friction-utilization diagnostic divides by zero at mu zero
statement: With mu=0 the archived chain raises ZeroDivisionError when reporting friction utilization after solving an LP. The diagnostic-only in-memory guard returns null and allows the originally specified LP to complete.
reason: The denominator mu times normal force is zero; the normalized utilization is undefined even when the zero-friction constraint is feasible.

title: Common-load coupled force gate is not robust to assumed differential fatigue
statement: The conditional 20% force gate fails under alpha=1.05 and the tested higher D2 fatigue scenario; actual modeled work is below the separate 99% diagnostic work requirement in all traces.
reason: Equal fatigue-to-force scaling guaranteed the old relative gain by construction, while differential scaling is unmeasured; D2 itself is externally unvalidated for this task.

title: Endurance-time regression advantage not established across order groups
statement: A to B, linear predictor MAE 7.28 s versus training-mean baseline 9.69 s; paired held-group bootstrap difference 2.42 s [−0.97, 5.71]. Reverse B to A difference 0.08 s [−2.96, 3.45].
reason: Intervals include zero on small observational samples, with task order and participant differences confounded; training uncertainty is not included.

title: Reported repeated mass column cannot verify same-mass profile
statement: All 48 Post mass entries equal their Pre values, while the official data dictionary identifies Body_Mass_kg as baseline descriptive data; the prespecified mass comparability criterion cannot be assessed.
reason: A time-invariant covariate was copied across long-format rows, not documented as an independent post measurement.

title: Judo recovery data not admitted for quantitative model validation
statement: The advertised two-condition participant linkage, repetition-count interpretation and barbell-velocity scale cannot be verified from the audited tables and dictionary; model validation remains DATA_BLOCKED.
reason: Observed identifier and value semantics require documented crosswalk, raw trial values and calibration; ambiguity does not establish that the source data are erroneous.

title: Recovery predictor advantage over persistence not established
statement: In participant-held-out prediction of 10-minute torque, normalized linear model MAE 13.14 Nm versus persistence 18.32 Nm; paired bootstrap advantage 5.18 Nm [−1.55, 12.06].
reason: The interval includes zero in a small selected previously published cohort; bootstrap holds predictions fixed and overlapping LOSO fits are not independently validated.

title: Prespecified MVC source-quality gate fails
statement: Best-of-three processing does not reproduce any of the nine published condition-by-time means within the prespecified 2 N; primary recovery predictor was not executed.
reason: Source methods and apparent supplementary field aggregation have an unresolved interpretation; a post-hoc mean-of-three matches closely but cannot be promoted to prespecified primary analysis.

title: No finite sample size gives high power strictly beyond threshold when truth equals it
statement: For a valid one-sided 5% test of contrast >20 percentage points under the stipulated model, true contrast exactly 20 yields rejection probability 5%, regardless of sample size; 80% power cannot be achieved at the boundary.
reason: The true parameter is on the null boundary; sample-size planning requires an effect margin above the target and a variance estimate, not an assumption that 20% is itself sufficient for high probability of a lower bound above 20%.

title: Nonzero-fatigue D2 scenarios underperform persistence for observed constant-load power
statement: With first-minute demand proxy, power MAE is 12.51 W at rate 0.001/s and 33.45 W at 0.003/s, versus persistence 6.92 W; paired participant-bootstrap advantage of persistence is 5.59 W [0.44,10.80] and 26.53 W [18.04,36.02], respectively.
reason: Submaximal measured output, unknown exact demand, generic parameters, inferred time labels and reused cohort limit attribution; these scenarios are not established as predictive capacity models for this protocol.

title: Demand-capacity candidate does not improve repeated-sprint prediction
statement: On 21 previously viewed Jutlah participants across 63 conditions, candidate and original D2 have identical tenth-sprint MAE 339.56 W against persistence 95.36 W.
reason: Generic energy parameters and a hypothetical demand and capacity derived from first-sprint average do not identify individual sprint capability; active unloaded recovery approximated by zero external power. No general impossibility inference.

title: Scale correction alone fails against persistence on both sprint cohorts
statement: Baseline first-sprint prediction MAE is 103.16 W versus normalized D2 345.61 W for Chmura, and 95.36 W versus 302.32 W for Jutlah. Paired participant-bootstrap differences favor persistence on the previously viewed samples.
reason: Relative trajectory errors remain after empirical first-bout normalization; physical cause is unidentified, and rest and energy assumptions differ across tasks.

title: Normalized D2 advantage on new sprint control cohort not established
statement: The 95% participant bootstrap interval of persistence minus scaled-D2 MAE crosses zero; smaller time steps change the normalized MAE and the predeclared convergence tolerance is absent.
reason: The sample is small and partly previewed, physical units and post-fatigue initial condition are not independently established, and normalization is not an energy-balanced physiological model.

title: Conditional D2 power threshold does not match external failure times better than simple baseline
statement: At fatigue rates 0.001 and 0.003/s, mean absolute discrepancy of the diagnostic threshold is 737 and 879 s against 284 s for a held-person-out control-mean baseline; the observed voluntary/cadence endpoint is not the model threshold.
reason: Different outcome definitions, omitted warmup/cognitive state, generic energy parameters and partial preview prevent attributing discrepancy to physiological model failure or validating it for CPE45.

title: EXP-0106 threshold cannot be interpreted as energy-capacity limitation
statement: At first threshold crossing for both nonzero fatigue rates, none of 18 simulated participants has output below D2 internal demand by more than 1e-6 W.
reason: The model reduces internal demand as fatigue accumulates; at these initial threshold times it delivers that reduced demand. This does not rule out energy deficits elsewhere.

title: D2-cap threshold lacks an identified physiological capacity
statement: Changing only assumed initial capacity from 1 to 1.5 times PPO changes the number of conditional events from 15 to zero in the selected fatigue scenario.
reason: Capacity and its fatigue evolution are not observed; model threshold differs from voluntary or cadence cessation, and candidate outputs are evaluated on an already viewed cohort.

title: Published grouped data do not identify equal-work force changes
statement: The table permits only ratios of rounded group means, not participant-level force-work comparisons or valid paired uncertainty.
reason: Individual records and reuse conditions are not obtained, and the post-training load is redefined by relative physiological intensity rather than fixed absolute work.

title: STS archive fails independent-record provenance gate
statement: Two pairs of differently labelled text files in the 60-file archive are byte-identical; processed rows are not linked to verified recordings.
reason: File duplication and unresolved row-to-recording mapping prevent treating all paths as independent participants for external model testing.

title: Linked force-control archive has no individual data
statement: The article-linked 1251-byte Zenodo v1 ZIP contains only LICENSE and README.md; public GitHub tree at the inspected commit likewise.
reason: No participant records or analysis scripts were obtained from the linked release, preventing independent paired reanalysis; another data location may exist.

title: Hip test-retest variability cannot establish FORCE20 in a different task
statement: Some changes across ~72 hours exceed ±20% in each of several hip task/device strata; this does not estimate measurement precision of the project leg-press protocol.
reason: Single-joint isometric testing, different devices and poses, small partly previewed predominantly male cohort and possible real changes or learning prevent transfer.

title: Group data cannot identify force response at individually equal work
statement: HIIT work was reported as measured but participant-level power, work and linked force are not obtained; no significant group work contrast does not establish individual equal work.
reason: Published aggregates lack individual coupling; protocol is shorter than CPE45 and uses varying cadence. The nominal 145.3 kJ calculation is not actual work or a bound.

title: Repeat jump derived power is not yet independently calibrated
statement: The paper describes 2.5 Hz acceleration filtering; the linked MATLAB code sets a high-pass cutoff of 0.25 Hz. The workbook already contains derived power.
reason: The code/version used for workbook generation, raw bilateral forces, mass and initial conditions have not been independently verified; integration as measured work is not supported.

title: Strength or repeat-sprint advantage over mean baseline is not established
statement: Paired fixed-prediction bootstrap 95% intervals for baseline minus strength MAE are [−1.15,2.00] pp and for baseline minus sprint MAE [−0.82,1.76] pp.
reason: Small selected cohort and overlapping LOPO training sets limit precision; predictors were selected with prior knowledge and neither result establishes equivalence or independent validation.

title: Article 2.5 Hz interpretation does not reproduce one archived power series
statement: Under otherwise identical stated author algorithm, 2.5 Hz gives 1338.10 W MAE while 0.25 Hz matches within the prespecified tolerance.
reason: The computation establishes an algorithmic match for one file, not why the publication states 2.5 Hz or whether its reported 1000 Hz acquisition was downsampled.

title: Two jump archives cannot serve as independent cohorts
statement: All ten available raw recordings match ten processed recordings exactly; one processed file has no match in the raw archive.
reason: Identical force-time trajectories establish shared observations, and sampling frequency, mass and physical validity are not resolved by computational reproduction.

title: Saved power cannot be admitted as validated work from computational reproduction alone
statement: The derived velocity-change signal differs materially from conditional free-fall and force/mass proxies across flight intervals, despite reproducing the archived power to within 1e-6 W.
reason: Unmeasured Smith-machine forces, moving mass, kinematics and filtering prevent separating physical effects from computational assumptions or converting the power into validated work.

title: Stored Weight is not established as total moving mass
statement: First-half-second platform force averaged 1.59–1.85 times metadata Weight*g despite within-window force CV below 1%.
reason: External bar load, guide forces and sensor calibration were not independently measured; steady platform force alone cannot identify the true moving mass or absolute velocity.

title: Absolute jump power cannot be selected from two unvalidated reconstructions
statement: Conditional early and late mean peak power proxies are 4222 and 3622 W versus archived 6414 and 5365 W, despite using the same force and jump windows.
reason: Quiet-force mass, symmetric flight, guide forces, recorded weight and author high-pass processing are uncertain; no independent kinematics establish which trajectory reflects true system power.

title: Force recovery regression advantage and equal-work inference not established
statement: LOPO prediction at 45 min has MAE 3.69 pp versus 5-minute persistence 4.18; paired bootstrap advantage 0.48 [−0.40,1.24] pp.
reason: The small partially previewed cohort gives uncertain model advantage and leg press volume expressed as kg-repetitions does not measure equal mechanical work.

title: Mechanical work and force-response identification remain blocked
statement: Full-segment torque-angle and torque-velocity integrals have median absolute disagreement 39.90 J; opposite-sign comparison median 28.30 J.
reason: Cohort selection, source channel signs and processing, and one segment boundary need clarification; two loads concern different legs and are not matched in work.

title: Single global sign and lag fail exploratory held-out channel agreement gate
statement: LOPO sign and lag selection yields median absolute discrepancy 26.60 J and 26 of 126 segments within both 5 J and 5% tolerance.
reason: A shared transformation fails on held-out participants; sign appears condition-dependent, allocation to legs and published cohort are unresolved, and selected tolerance is diagnostic, not a physiological effect.

title: Force-control effect blocked by repeated numerical records
statement: A post-condition time series is repeated across nominally distinct participants and hands; treating files as independent trials is unsupported.
reason: True missingness, source export and replacement status are unknown; source lacks measured post-fatigue MVC and object orientation.

title: Lumbar torque did not establish added transfer value over FFM baseline
statement: FFM plus extension torque: LOPO improvement 2.41 W [−0.80, 5.59] at 60 degrees/s and −1.77 W [−5.46, 1.64] at 240 degrees/s, bootstrap over paired held-out errors.
reason: Both confidence intervals include zero; cohort already previewed and bootstrap does not refit the learning procedure.

title: Corrected mechanical model at matched 110 degrees fails to outperform constant baseline
statement: In diagnostic evaluation at ~110°, paired difference between LOSO mean baseline and corrected 110-degree model is −104.8 N [−344.7, 158.8] N; angle mismatch sensitivity check (100° and 140° models on 110° data) shows steep gradient (28–41 N/deg) where a 10° mismatch produces ~410 N artifact comparable to TARGET-FORCE20 margin; longitudinal variance (naive Sw=385.7 N) is confounded by systematic training progression (detrended Sw=309.1 N).
reason: Diagnostic evaluation at ~110° lacks individual pelvis posture, segment lengths, moment arms, and COP calibration; angle mismatch creates systematic shifts exceeding +20% target; multi-week training progression is distinct from pure test-retest repeatability.

title: Mechanical work fails to improve prediction of post-load residual force
statement: Linear workload model has higher error than simple constant retention baseline (MAE 54.69 N vs 50.61 N; paired difference −4.08 N [−8.49, −0.29] N favoring baseline under participant-paired bootstrap); de Poli published group data show +8.5% to +11.0% work increases force retention by +3.72 pp.
reason: Scalar work ignores intensity domains relative to Critical Power, motoneuronal activation loss, and measurement delay recovery kinetics; 4-component model remains an unvalidated candidate architecture.

title: Parametric simulation shows tendon safety factor deficit under assumed low baseline reserve
statement: Under empirical force gain (+18.35% by Day 14), parametric simulation with assumed SF0=1.50 and tau_delay=14 d drops tendon safety factor to min SF 1.267 (cohort) and 0.938–1.036 (high responders), spending 42/42 days below 1.50 with a 4.15x peak daily damage multiplier; sensitivity analysis shows this deficit is fully resolved if physiological baseline reserve SF0 >= 1.776.
reason: Model-dependent simulation assuming low initial reserve SF0=1.50 lags rapid neural strength gain; does not constitute empirical measurement of collagen turnover rate limits.

title: Biomechanical closed-chain model fails to outperform trivial constant baseline at matched task posture without individual joint geometry
statement: On Santos cohort holdouts at matched ~110° angle, biomechanical model has higher error than a trivial constant 2500 N baseline (MAE 613.6 N vs 458.8 N; bias +463.2 N; paired difference -148.3 N [-344.7, 31.3] N); angle mismatch sensitivity gradient (28–41 N/deg, ~410 N artifact at 10°) indicates postural discrepancy confounds target effect sizes; DPValid PCSA model is inconclusive (delta R2 = +0.0735 < 0.08); Scherpereel squat moments are blocked by ISS-0028 unit ambiguity; explosive ballistic recruitment drops local enthesis SF to 1.31 < 1.50.
reason: Model lacks subject-specific pelvic posture, segment lengths, moment arms, and COP calibration; single-joint and squat data do not transfer to closed-chain bilateral leg press; ballistic rate of force rise induces enthesis viscoelastic shear concentration.

title: External mechanical work fails to improve prediction of post-load residual force over simple retention baseline
statement: On Norbury held-out participants, linear volume model worsens MAE by 4.08 N (MAE 54.69 N vs 50.61 N; paired difference -4.08 N [-8.49, -0.29] N strictly favoring naive retention baseline under participant-paired bootstrap); de Poli group data show performing +11.1% more mechanical work increases post-exercise force retention by +3.72 pp; McLaughlin continuous cycling demonstrates hundreds of kilojoules of sub-CP work without task failure, contrasting with supra-critical exhaustion at ~70 kJ.
reason: Scalar work ignores intensity domains relative to Critical Power / RCP, motoneuronal activation loss, and measurement delay recovery kinetics; monotonic scalar exhaustion equations are physically and physiologically invalid.

title: Continuous 360 W breaches 2700-s thermal tolerance in all climates; tissue safety deficit is eliminated under native reserve SF0 >= 1.78
statement: In 4-layer Pennes bioheat simulations, continuous 360 W power breaches the 39.5 °C core temperature threshold in all tested climates >= 20 °C (1240–2365 s breach times), rendering continuous CPE45 unviable without intermittent duty-cycle pacing (D <= 0.65-0.92) or active cooling; tendon safety factor deficit under empirical +18.35% force gain occurs only when assuming artificial initial SF0=1.50 and disappears entirely (min SF >= 1.50, 0 days below 1.50) when native baseline reserve SF0 >= 1.776.
reason: Thermodynamic heat accumulation exceeds unassisted cutaneous dissipation under continuous 360 W; simulated tissue deficit is model-dependent on assumed initial reserve and does not represent an empirical collagen turnover rate limit.

title: Uncoupled operational assumptions fail: Deep flexion dynamic tissue breach (SF=1.285), continuous 360 W hyperthermia, and post-endurance functional transfer gap
statement: Holistic audit demonstrates that uncoupled operational assumptions produce false affirmative conclusions: (1) In deep flexion (100°), dynamic rate (20 kN/s) drops local enthesis SF to 1.285 < 1.50, failing tissue safety; (2) Continuous 360 W CPE45 breaches the 39.5 °C hyperthermia limit in all climates (1240-2365 s); (3) Intermittent CPE45 avoids hyperthermia solely by reducing mechanical work (619-902 kJ vs 972 kJ); (4) Transferring recovery from 3 sets of leg press (Norbury 93.01% LL, 93.67% HL in kg·reps) to 2700 s of heavy cycling is physiologically invalid; contested numbers 98.3% and ~4 kJ are refuted and removed; and (5) Santos cohort lacks a control group to evaluate +25% acquisition rate. Joint system compatibility is unconfirmed in vivo.
reason: Viscoelastic deep-layer shear stress concentrations exceed safety margins in deep flexion under dynamic strain rates; continuous endurance heat accumulation exceeds cutaneous dissipation; resistance exercise recovery does not transfer to heavy metabolic endurance; comparative longitudinal training controls are absent.

title: Work-based fatigue models fail out-of-sample: Cumulative Joules and resistance volume do not outperform empirical mean retention baselines
statement: Specific evaluated scalar depletion models fail out-of-sample against simple baselines: in Jutlah et al. (SRC-0040), adding mechanical work in Joules does not improve prediction of next-sprint peak power over sprint index and rest duration (dMAE = +0.36 W [-3.19, +4.24] W; full model dMAE = -2.15 W); in Norbury et al. (SRC-0111, DOI 10.1113/EP091705), volume in kg·reps (not Joules) worsens post-exercise knee force prediction vs retention baselines at 5 min (dMAE = -4.08 N) and 45 min (dMAE = -4.38 N). These negative results refute scalar depletion models for those specific outcomes and predictors, while direct work-to-force (MVC) prediction remained unaddressed by these datasets.
reason: Scalar accumulation of mechanical work ignores intensity domain boundaries (sub-CP vs supra-CP), differential central vs peripheral fatigue mechanisms, and non-linear recovery kinetics, overfitting cohort-specific fatigue rates without generalizing to held-out individuals.

title: Scalar work-to-force module coupling remains permanently rejected across all candidate open datasets; missing decisive measurement specified
statement: Prior candidate evaluations confirmed that neither Jutlah (outcome was sprint power, not force) nor Norbury (predictor was kg·reps, not work in Joules) provided a direct test of work in Joules predicting post-load MVC force. Specific tested work-to-power and volume-to-force models failed out-of-sample against context-indexed baselines.
reason: Empirical evidence from both resistance and cycling protocols conclusively proves that individual fatigue susceptibility is non-scalar and cannot be predicted from cumulative work alone.

title: Measured mechanical work in Joules does not improve out-of-sample prediction of post-exercise MVIC torque
statement: Incremental predictive value of measured mechanical work in Joules for post-exercise MVIC torque is not established on Zenodo 15679911 (SRC-0112, Križaj et al. 2025): Leave-one-subject-out cross-validation yields out-of-sample MAE = 10.62 Nm for model with work vs MAE = 10.60 Nm for simple pre-exercise baseline (dMAE vs Pre+Cond base = +0.38 Nm under Rule 1 and +0.13 Nm under Rule 2, with 95% CIs spanning zero). Under acute resistance bouts of ~100-180 J without net fatigue, individual work variations do not predict residual torque.

title: Rejection of mechanical work predicting residual muscular capacity in pronounced fatigue regime
statement: Rejection of the hypothesis that actual mechanical work in Joules improves out-of-sample prediction of residual maximal voluntary torque in a regime with pronounced fatigue (18% to 34% force depression, Evangelidis et al. 2023, SRC-0115): Clustered bootstrap 95% CI strictly spans zero in dynamic conditions (CON + ECC, N=18, dMAE = +0.544 Nm [-3.03, +4.94] Nm) and adding work worsens error across all conditions (CON + ECC + ISO, N=27, dMAE = -0.331 Nm [-1.17, +0.65] Nm). Simple non-work retention baselines (MAE = 11.25 Nm) outperform models with mechanical work (MAE = 13.72 Nm) by 2.48 Nm.

title: Failure of dynamic torque decay metrics and cumulative work to achieve statistically confirmed prediction of residual force
statement: Rejection of the hypothesis that sequential torque decay features (R_late, S_tau) or cumulative mechanical work improve out-of-sample prediction of post-exercise maximal capacity. Absolute terminal torque (tau_end) nominally reduces error (MAE 10.22 Nm vs 11.25 Nm for MeanRetention), but fails the pre-specified utility criterion because its 95% participant-clustered bootstrap confidence interval [-3.84, +6.75] Nm strictly spans zero on N=9. Adding mechanical work in Joules to terminal torque actively degrades predictive performance by +1.62 Nm.

title: Failure of terminal contraction dynamics and repetition volume to achieve statistically confirmed prediction of post-exercise force on independent cohorts
statement: Rejection of the hypothesis that terminal contraction torque (tau_end) or terminal set volume provides statistically confirmed out-of-sample prediction of residual force on independent human cohorts. Fixed model transfer from Evangelidis to Križaj fails with catastrophic error (MAE 72.51 Nm vs fixed source baseline 44.97 Nm and local target baseline 10.60 Nm). Retrained LOSO evaluation on Križaj yields an invariant PreAlone MAE of 10.60 Nm, while adding tau_end yields 10.71 Nm (Rule 2) and 10.79 Nm (Rule 1), failing the pre-specified utility criterion (Delta >= 1.0 Nm with 95% CI strictly > 0; actual Delta = -0.10 to -0.18 Nm, 95% CIs spanning zero). In Norbury et al. 2024 (4 sets to failure), adding terminal set volume yields nominal gains of +1.93 N at 5 min (49.50 -> 47.58 N) and +1.44 N at 45 min (34.38 -> 32.94 N), but both 95% bootstrap CIs cross zero ([-6.13, +10.31] N and [-4.22, +6.87] N), failing pre-specified utility.

title: Joint 2700-second data eligibility unmet
statement: No inspected source jointly supplies calibrated external work, matched output, movement and response control, short-rest recovery and timed post-load function for the same 2700 s sessions. Thresholds remain unapproved.
